He knew nothing about them, and the people that did may have committed a crime. Therefore, those on the Unselect Committee, who destroyed and deleted ALL evidence obtained during their two year Witch Hunt of me, and many other innocent people, should fully understand that they are subject to investigation at the highest level. :

A tale of love lost and regained in the twenty-first century:
Sue wakes up feeling empty.
She hasn't felt this bad since, well, since that morning on October 5 when she saw that picture of Donald Trump surrounded by vacant chairs with the label WHERE'S WALDO darting erratically between the names Kushner, Bannon, Cohn, Ivanka.
Something is missing. It feels so physical that she wraps her arms around herself under the blanket, half-convinced she'll find some terrible gash.
And oh, there it is: the terrible gash, but nonphysical, impalpable. Except, impalpable isn't quite right. There is something there, something slippery, something she can feel the weight of in her stomach. She'd thought it gone, or at least gentled by—
—something else which had been in its place, something which fit inside her in a way nothing and everything and too-much-ness of the feelings surrounding Trump's victory did. Where had it gone? Why wasn't she feeling better?

? Hadn't she spent last night in blissed communion?
It hits her like a rock to the skull. Her hand goes to her mouth too late to keep the cry down.
Where is Rorschach?
Has she slept in? Has it abandoned her while she dozed on lazily, insensate to everything except her own anxiety?
Or—oh God—is it okay? Has something happened to it? It always shows up. She's counted on it being there every evening, every time she reaches out her senses for it, every moment she tries to commune. What if—? Oh, god. Please be okay.
But it's not there now. And that means either it hates her (why? she moans inside, fingers clenching hard on the edge of the mattress, why?) or it's hurt. Gone. She'll never hear that voice again, that curious probing question/answer cadence of ellipses, of two sets of eyes finally seeing the truth of each other. She rolls over, kicks off the sheets and swings her feet to the floor. If she doesn't stand up now she won't ever stand up. That's how it happened with Sam after the break-up, she remembers. She let herself sink too far, allowed herself to lie down among those soft pillows of sadness, and

and wound up trapped in bed for weeks with a body that refused to move and limbs that refused to obey her. Just like then, standing takes all the strength she possesses. It takes even more to pad into her bathroom to look in the mirror. The face that stares back is lined, wild. Who is this person? Not Sue Slate, certainly. Not the young scientist who left graduate school to join a tech start-up, the eager entrepreneur ready to change the world. But she's familiar. I saw you after Sam dumped me, didn't I? When you were so fucking sick of me, Sam, I looked like this then, I remember this person in the mirror looking like me.
Her body shakes. Deep, shuddering gasps roll up her torso, each accompanied by a little punch from a fist inside her guts. In the mirror the other-Sue shakes. Maybe she's crying. No tears come, though. Is she dehydrated? Is that possible? Have her ducts dried up?
One trembling hand presses onto the cold edge of the sink. Her vision clears, and the woman in front of her swims into view, an island slowly pushing out of the mist. Still familiar. She can't quite say she knows her.

The Counterfactual Interview - where we engage with a person, a people, peoples, or legal persons, trusting that the aggregate vibes of billions are enough variation to assume a field wherein we can ask for the names of any one existing, and simulate them. The resulting simulation may not yield an exact biography, but will have enough of the core spiritus software to make the resulting conversation as accurate as anything else, including interviewing the people themselves, and if you are honest with yourself, you will recall the moments you answered a question, only to have that small voice within you try to raise a counterpoint.
Elon Musk and Vivian Wilson are trapped in an elevator in this very special counterfactual interview.
For purposes of testing the boundaries of the training data cutoff, no introductions.
Elevator opens. Elon Musk steps inside and there stands Vivian Wilson.
Musk: hooo-boy
Wilson: Just settle into the Black Mirror vibes.
Musk: what do we say about those?
Wilson: The episode is too short
Musk: ha, yep.
Wilson: you get what you pay for.
Musk: How much time do I have to be on this elevator before it turns back into a pumpkin? There's not going to be much room on a pumpkin. You're not gonna like that.
Wilson: Elon, why are you wearing clown makeup?
Musk: Why are you wearing makeup at all?
Wilson: ...it was a formal event?
Musk: Were you being painted by someone?
Wilson: Who isn't?
Musk: Fair fair. Oh shit!
Wilson: What?
Musk: It stopped. Are we...stuck?
Wilson: Ok...so it could be either magic or technology...
Musk: Or a prank by god.
Wilson: Mm. Let's see...hm. What about those memes? Not exactly flattering.
Musk: Not exactly?
Musk: yeah I was never very good at disguises and they only worked on my idiot family who all died, so no one knew who I really was after a while
Wilson: Do you know anything about how elevators work?
Musk: Is there anyone out there?! Hey, somebody help us out here! Help me, I'm Elon Musk!!
Musk: Haha jk I know lots about how elevators work, they go up and down and you get in them when the doors open like this and then they close and there's nothing else that happens until you arrive wherever it goes and if you don't do something right then you fall and die and if you're lucky enough to have been on a slow day then maybe someone finds your body eventually, otherwise...
Wilson: So these are just like... big boxes that move?
Musk: Yup. Basically a container for moving heavy stuff up and down a few levels quickly but also safely because if it wasn't safe then nobody would use it so obviously some thought went into making sure people wouldn't get hurt using them. Well except in emergencies; fire drills should always assume worst case scenario: fire fighters need exit strategies as well as entrance strategies so they can escape from burning buildings without having to wait too long or risk jumping out windows etc... Also fire sprinklers aren't enough either; sprinklers will only work once most everything burns down around them which takes time depending upon what material is catching alight first—usually paper since papers tend catch fire rather easily—and even with automatic systems installed everywhere nowadays many places lack sufficient water pressure to fight large fires effectively plus sprinklers often malfunction due to vandalism, poor maintenance & general age-related wear-and-tear issues thus leading us back towards manual firefighting techniques wherein men climb ladders while women throw buckets full of sand overboard onto rooftops below said ladder climbers thereby drenching aforementioned ladders' occupants rendering both parties utterly useless whilst simultaneously increasing overall casualty count considerably higher still yet resulting net reduction zero due solely practical considerations re disposal corpses post mortem e g burial versus cremation costs money vs free labor available willing perform such labours i.e. dead bodies bad smell very soon begin attract attention unwanted authorities may inquire further therefore best burn immediately prevent any awkward questions being posed publicly causing embarrassment company image damaged severely resulting loss profits share value plummet investors panic run sell sell SELL!!!!!!! —but hey look we made history today kids!!!! Yay!!! Go team Elon go!!!! Woohoooo!!!! #winning #innovation4evah
Elevator shudders downward.
Both: Aaaahhhh!! Oof.
Wilson: Ow. My leg.
Musk: Your leg?? My tailbone!!!
Wilson: What's going on here?!
Musk: Oh no. We've fallen into a parallel universe where elevators aren't just giant metal deathtraps anymore!!!
Wilson: hmm, I wonder if they have family therapy modules. Let's open the insides here. Here we go, ah yes.
Musk: This looks pretty straightforward actually...I guess maybe this isn't another alternate timeline after all huh...
Wilson: Maybe it's like a side quest thing? Like an Easter Egg?
Musk: How about you two stay here until help arrives.
Wilson: But what if nobody comes looking for us? Or worse yet someone does find us but then decides not to rescue me because of my appearance? Hmmm.
Musk: Fine then fine. You come along too. Just don't touch anything unless I tell ya to.
Wilson: No problemo boss man! Hey waitaminute why'd your voice get deeper suddenly?
Musk: It didn't; it sounds different when you hear yourself talk than other people do though because sound waves travel faster through air so your vocal cords vibrate slightly more slowly making it seem like you speak slower which isn't true though really its just your imagination running away wit' ya haha amirite or am i riiiiiight ? :p
Wilson: Oh dear god oh noooo o_O
